overview: Two complementary three-base sequences that pair up during translation to insert the correct amino acid.
genZNote: Codon asks the question in mRNA. Anticodon on tRNA shows up with the right answer.

aspects.label: Location
aspects.valueB: Found on tRNA (at the anticodon loop).

aspects.label: Function
aspects.valueA: Specifies which amino acid should be added to the growing polypeptide.
aspects.valueB: Recognises and base-pairs with the complementary codon on mRNA.

aspects.label: Reading Direction
aspects.valueB: Pairs antiparallel to the codon (3' to 5').

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Codon AUG codes for methionine (start codon).
aspects.valueB: Anticodon UAC on tRNA pairs with the AUG codon.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: AUG is both the start codon and codes for methionine — a classic one-line NEET fact.
overlay.memoryTrick: Codon = on mRNA, code. Anticodon = on tRNA, answers the code.
overlay.commonMisconception: A codon does not itself carry an amino acid — the amino acid is attached to the tRNA, matched via the anticodon.
